title: AgentDocker Agentfile
description: Several agents described together and started with `agentdocker up`. Put `#:schema <this file's URL>` on the first line of an Agentfile.toml for completion and checking in a TOML editor. `agentdocker agentfile check` reads a file the way `up` will.

version.description: The Agentfile format version. Absent means 1, the format before versions. Version 2 adds the launch fields (prompt, effort, args, config, idle_messages, coordinate) and expands ${VAR}; `agentdocker agentfile upgrade` rewrites a version 1 file.

name.description: Team name: every agent gets the label team=<name>.

agents.description: The agents, by name, started in the order written except that one starts after what it waits on.

expandable.description: From version 2, ${VAR}, ${VAR:-default}, ${VAR-default}, ${VAR:?message} and ${VAR?message} are expanded from the environment of the `up` that reads the file, and $$ is one dollar sign; any other $ is an error.

runtime.description: What hosts the agent. From version 2 a command can be built (from prompt, model, effort, config) for claude-code, codex and gemini-cli; any other runtime needs `command`.

provider.description: The model provider, a label for `ps`.

model.description: The model. Passed to the runtime when agentdocker builds the command; a label for `ps` on a written command.

command.description: The command line, launched as written. Required in version 1; from version 2 it may be left out for a runtime agentdocker builds a command for, and then must be.

workdir.description: Where the agent runs; relative to the Agentfile's directory.

isolate.description: Give the agent its own linked worktree and branch.

tty.description: Give the agent a terminal rather than pipes, for an interactive runtime; `agentdocker attach` reaches it.

restore.description: Bring the agent back under the same identity when agentd restarts.

in_pane.description: Run the agent in a tmux pane, reachable with `tmux attach`.

restart.description: When to start it again after it exits.

depends_on.description: Agents in this file that must be running before this one starts.

after.description: Agents in this file that must have exited with status zero before this one starts: "build exits 0", or a list of such conditions. If one ends any other way, this agent is never started, and nor is anything waiting on it.

prompt.description: Version 2. The first instruction, for a command agentdocker builds. Without a terminal (tty, in_pane) it is required, except for Codex with idle_messages, which takes none on its command line.

effort.description: Version 2. Reasoning effort in the runtime's words: claude-code low, medium, high, xhigh, max; codex minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh; Gemini CLI has none. A ${VAR} here is checked once expanded.

args.description: Version 2. The runtime's own arguments, added to a built command before the prompt. A model or effort set here is left as given.

config.description: Version 2. The runtime's own settings, given the way it takes them: Claude Code's `--settings` as one JSON document, Codex's `-c key=value` per leaf (a nested table is a dotted key, so `approval_policy = "never"` or `sandbox = { mode = "workspace-write" }` both read); Gemini CLI takes none. Strings in it expand ${VAR}.

idle_messages.description: Version 2. Let a message start a turn while the session is idle: Claude Code's channel (an interactive session; Claude's consent applies) or Codex's input adapter (which then takes no prompt on its command line). Experimental.

coordinate.description: Version 2. Wire AgentDocker into a built command: the MCP server (and, for Claude Code, the hooks) unless the runtime's own configuration already has them.
